method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, formula/token comparison, rule-direction inspection and reverse paraphrase with a freshly rechecked official Marathi Vishwakosh proof-theory passage; not independent or human review.
scope: The sequent-calculus overview: sequents, derivation trees and rules, the induced derivability relation and theoremhood, inconsistency and weakening, and Gentzen's historical contribution and the calculus's practical strengths and limitations.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section introduces sequent calculus. A sequent is a pair of sentence sequences separated by the sequent symbol, and either side may be empty. A derivation is a tree of sequents whose top nodes are initial sequents or axioms and whose remaining nodes follow from immediately preceding sequents by inference rules. Rules either manipulate sentences on the left or right or introduce a complex formula in their conclusion; the displayed conjunction-left and conditional-right examples preserve their stated premise and conclusion.
samples.checks: The pair structure, ordered sides, empty-side allowance, tree orientation, initial-sequent synonym, immediate-parent restriction and both example-rule directions are preserved. Every displayed and inline formula, macro and index token has exact parity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma proves A exactly when some sequence Gamma-zero consists only of members of Gamma and a derivation has Gamma-zero sequent A at its root. A is a theorem when the empty-left sequent A has a derivation. The proof tree derives the conditional from a conjunction-left step followed by a conditional-right step.
samples.checks: The biconditional retains both directions; the Gamma-zero subset condition, root condition, empty-premise theorem condition and proof-tree order are explicit. The two occurrences of Gamma-zero in the defining prose and every prooftree command remain unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma is inconsistent when a derivation ends in a sequent with some Gamma-zero drawn from Gamma on the left and an empty right side. Right weakening then permits any sentence to be derived from an inconsistent set.
samples.checks: The empty right side is not confused with an empty premise set; Gamma-zero remains restricted to members of Gamma; the weakening direction and explosion consequence are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gerhard Gentzen invented sequent calculus in the 1930s. Its systematic symmetric design makes it useful for developing a theory of derivations. Derivations are comparatively easy to find but often hard to read and relate to proofs. The approach is elegant and has versions for many logics.
samples.checks: The inventor, decade, systematic and symmetric qualities, metatheoretic purpose, discovery-versus-readability contrast and broad availability claim are all retained. The official Marathi Vishwakosh independently attests गरहार्ड गेंटझेन and क्रमवर्ती कलन.

source_observations.finding: The frozen source comment spells the section identifier as ‘seqeunt-calculus’. It is non-rendered metadata and is preserved byte-for-byte in the target.
The frozen sentence ‘their connection to proofs are sometimes not easy to see’ has ordinary subject-verb disagreement. The Marathi conveys the unambiguous intended meaning without changing the claim.

limitations: No independent linguistic review has been performed.

क्रमवर्ती कलन and गरहार्ड गेंटझेन are directly attested in the checked official Marathi proof-theory article, but standalone क्रमवर्ती is a definition-controlled nominalization of the attested compound rather than a directly attested noun.
The target therefore records standalone क्रमवर्ती as provisional and exposes सिक्वेंट, क्रमवर्ती अभिव्यक्ती and अनुक्रमिका for specialist comparison.
